GitHub community setup (maintainer)

Source: .github/COMMUNITY_SETUP.md

Repository files provide contributor guidance and templates; they do not change GitHub settings. Apply the settings below manually as repository administrator. No remote changes were made as part of this setup.

Observed state

Read-only inspection on 2026-10-21 found:

  • Default branch: main; Issues and Discussions are enabled.
  • Private Vulnerability Reporting: disabled (enabled: false).
  • The five established labels in the table below already exist. The other three requested labels are missing.
  • The branch endpoint marks main as protected, but its embedded classic protection data reports disabled enforcement and no required checks. This does not establish the effective ruleset configuration; inspect it in Settings before changing anything.
  • The repository metadata available to this inspection did not expose merge method settings. Verify them in Settings.

Recheck current state before configuring; this is a dated observation.

Security reporting and Discussions

  1. In Settings > Advanced Security, enable Private vulnerability reporting. Confirm the private report form is available. Update the dated disabled-status paragraph in SECURITY.md after enabling it.
  2. Keep Discussions enabled under Settings > General > Features for questions, usage help, and early ideas. Keep Issues enabled for bug reports and concrete proposals.

Private reporting must be enabled for the security link in the issue chooser to accept reports. Never redirect sensitive reports to public Issues or Discussions. See GitHub’s private reporting configuration guide.

Merge and branch protection

  • Under Settings > General > Pull Requests, allow Squash and merge and disable merge commits and rebase merging. Each accepted PR should produce one meaningful commit on main.
  • Review existing rules under Settings > Rules > Rulesets and Branches. Protect main against deletion and force pushes, and require PRs for external changes. Avoid overlapping or contradictory protection rules.
  • Require successful checks from the existing R-CMD-check workflow: the six OS/R matrix jobs, CRAN incoming (R-devel, built tarball), SQL integration (DBI + SQLite), both PTY integration jobs, and Windows input regressions. Require the pkgdown build for documentation validation as well. Select the exact check names displayed on a recent PR; do not guess their workflow prefixes. All these workflows run on ordinary PRs to main.
  • Do not require worker-probe or pre-rc-targeted-diagnostics: they run on demand or special branches and would leave ordinary PRs waiting forever.
  • Require one maintainer approval for external PRs. Give the sole maintainer an explicit bypass for their own PRs (for example, the repository administrator role with a ruleset bypass limited to pull requests). GitHub does not allow authors to approve their own PRs. Verify this path works before enforcing the rule; avoid requiring approval of the latest push by another person. Use the bypass only to satisfy the unavailable second-person review on the maintainer’s own PRs, after checking the diff and successful CI.
  • Keep write access limited to the maintainer; contributing does not confer merge permissions. External PRs need the maintainer’s review and acceptance.

See GitHub’s ruleset reference. Do not introduce new Actions for labels or routine governance.

Labels

Preserve all existing unrelated labels, including accessibility, duplicate, invalid, question, and wontfix. Keep the existing five definitions unchanged and add only the three missing labels:

Label Color (hex) Description Observed state
bug d73a4a Something isn’t working Exists; preserve
enhancement a2eeef New feature or request Exists; preserve
documentation 0075ca Improvements or additions to documentation Exists; preserve
good first issue 7057ff Good for newcomers Exists; preserve
help wanted 008672 Extra attention is needed Exists; preserve
needs reproduction d4c5f9 More information or a reproducible example is needed Create
needs discussion fbca04 Maintainer discussion is needed before implementation Create
breaking change b60205 Incompatible change requiring prior discussion and release planning Create

The bug and feature forms automatically apply bug and enhancement, respectively. All other labels are assigned manually. GitHub requires form labels to exist; both automatic labels were confirmed present.

The following commands are proposals for an authorized administrator to run, not automation. GitHub CLI is optional; the labels UI can make the same changes. First inspect current labels:

gh label list --repo menshikovs/termr --limit 100

Create the three missing labels if they are still absent:

gh label create "needs reproduction" --repo menshikovs/termr --color d4c5f9 --description "More information or a reproducible example is needed"
gh label create "needs discussion" --repo menshikovs/termr --color fbca04 --description "Maintainer discussion is needed before implementation"
gh label create "breaking change" --repo menshikovs/termr --color b60205 --description "Incompatible change requiring prior discussion and release planning"

No command uses --force or deletes existing labels. See the GitHub CLI label reference.

After these files reach main, preview the issue chooser and both forms, confirm automatic labels on a legitimate report, and confirm that PRs pick up the template. Local validation cannot exercise GitHub’s hosted form renderer.
